major_error_concepts: Treating nucleotide excision and base excision as identical substrate-recognition mechanisms.
cards.prompt: What is Nucleotide Excision Repair? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Excise a lesion-containing nucleotide segment.
Resynthesis and sealing restore continuity.

cards.definition: Homologous recombination repair uses a homologous DNA template to restore information at a break or related lesion. Template availability and cell-cycle context influence its use and outcome.
major_error_concepts: Claiming homologous recombination needs no matching sequence template.
cards.prompt: What is Homologous Recombination Repair? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Homologous template guides repair.
Context and template choice matter.

cards.definition: Nonhomologous end joining repairs a DNA double-strand break by reconnecting ends without requiring extensive homologous template sequence. End processing can introduce changes, though outcomes depend on the particular break and pathway.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every end-joining event copies an intact homologous chromosome.
cards.prompt: What is Nonhomologous End Joining? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: End joining without extensive homology.
Processing can be mutagenic but not every join has the same outcome.

cards.definition: A DNA-damage checkpoint is a signaling response that detects damage or replication stress and coordinates cell-cycle progression with repair or other responses. Arrest is a regulated response, not the repair chemistry itself.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a checkpoint directly fills every damaged DNA gap.
cards.prompt: What is DNA-Damage Checkpoint? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Damage signaling coordinates cell-cycle behavior.
Checkpoint signaling differs from lesion repair.

cards.definition: Replication licensing establishes origins competent to initiate replication during an appropriate cell-cycle window. Eukaryotic controls separating licensing from firing help prevent repeated copying of the same DNA within one cycle.
major_error_concepts: Assuming each licensed origin necessarily fires in every cell cycle.
cards.prompt: What is Replication Licensing? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Prepare origins for regulated initiation.
Separate licensing and activation to avoid rereplication.

cards.definition: A telomere is the specialized nucleoprotein structure at a linear chromosome end. It helps protect the end from inappropriate repair and participates in managing end-replication limitations.
major_error_concepts: Treating every telomere as an unprotected broken chromosome end.
cards.prompt: What is Telomere? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Protective linear chromosome-end structure.
Distinct from an accidental double-strand break.

cards.definition: Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme using an internal RNA template to extend telomeric DNA. Its activity varies among cells and organisms and does not imply unlimited healthy proliferation by itself.
major_error_concepts: Claiming telomerase copies an entire chromosome or is equally active in every cell.
cards.prompt: What is Telomerase? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: RNA-templated telomeric DNA extension.

cards.definition: DNA denaturation separates paired strands by disrupting noncovalent duplex interactions without necessarily cleaving the covalent backbone. Sequence, length, and environmental conditions influence duplex stability.
major_error_concepts: Equating denaturation with phosphodiester-chain digestion.
cards.prompt: What is DNA Denaturation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Separate paired strands rather than cut the backbone.

cards.definition: Nucleic-acid hybridization forms base-paired associations between sufficiently complementary strands or regions. Pairing specificity depends on sequence and conditions and can tolerate some mismatches.
major_error_concepts: Assuming one mismatch always prevents every hybridization event.
cards.prompt: What is Nucleic-Acid Hybridization? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Complementarity-driven strand association.
Specificity depends on context.

cards.definition: RNA stability describes how long a transcript persists before degradation. Steady-state abundance reflects both production and decay, so a stable transcript can remain abundant even without a high current synthesis rate.
major_error_concepts: Treating abundance as identical to transcription rate regardless of decay.
cards.prompt: What is RNA Stability? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Persistence or decay kinetics.
Abundance combines synthesis and removal.

accepted_variants: The start phase of protein synthesis.
cards.definition: Translation initiation assembles a ribosome, initiator tRNA, and associated factors at an appropriate start site. It establishes the reading frame and is a major regulatory step, with mechanisms differing between organisms.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any ribosome can begin at any arbitrary triplet with no initiation signals.
cards.prompt: What is Translation Initiation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Assembly at a start site establishes the frame.
Mechanisms are system-dependent.

cards.definition: Protein targeting directs a polypeptide to an appropriate cellular compartment or destination through sequence features and recognition machinery. Targeting can occur during or after translation and may involve signal cleavage.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all proteins remain in the compartment where translation begins.
cards.prompt: What is Protein Targeting? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Signals and machinery specify destination.
Timing and processing vary.

accepted_variants: The renewal and degradation dynamics of proteins.
cards.definition: Protein turnover is the combined synthesis and degradation of a protein population. Protein abundance can change through either process, and half-life describes decay under an appropriate kinetic model.
major_error_concepts: Inferring synthesis rate directly from a single abundance measurement.
cards.prompt: What is Protein Turnover? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Production and removal jointly shape abundance.

cards.definition: The proteasome is a protein complex that degrades selected polypeptides, often after recognition of an appropriate ubiquitin signal in eukaryotic cells. It is one degradation route, not the mechanism for all cellular protein removal.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every protein is degraded exclusively by the proteasome.
cards.prompt: What is Proteasome? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Selective protein-degradation complex.
Not the only degradation pathway.

cards.definition: Ubiquitin is a small protein covalently attached to substrates through an enzyme cascade. Different ubiquitin configurations can signal degradation, trafficking, or other regulation; ubiquitination does not always mean destruction.
major_error_concepts: Equating every ubiquitin attachment with immediate proteasomal degradation.
cards.prompt: What is Ubiquitin? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Covalent protein modification with varied signaling outcomes.

cards.definition: A riboswitch is an RNA element that binds a ligand and changes structure to regulate expression. It can couple metabolite recognition directly to transcriptional or translational control without a separate protein receptor for that sensing step.
major_error_concepts: Defining every riboswitch as a DNA-binding protein.
cards.prompt: What is Riboswitch? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Ligand-binding RNA changes expression through structural response.

cards.definition: RNA interference uses small guide RNAs and effector proteins to recognize target sequences and reduce gene expression through RNA cleavage, repression, or related pathways. Its implementation varies across organisms and RNA classes.
major_error_concepts: Claiming RNA interference always deletes the corresponding genomic gene.
cards.prompt: What is RNA Interference? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Guide-RNA-directed sequence recognition and silencing.

cards.definition: Alternative polyadenylation selects different transcript cleavage and poly(A)-addition sites. It can change three-prime UTR length or coding content and thereby alter regulation without changing the genome sequence.
major_error_concepts: Assuming it only changes the number of adenines in an otherwise identical transcript tail.
cards.prompt: What is Alternative Polyadenylation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Alternative RNA three-prime processing sites.
Can change regulatory or coding content.

accepted_variants: Export of mature or selected nuclear transcripts.
cards.definition: Nuclear RNA export transports selected RNA-protein complexes from the nucleus to the cytoplasm through regulated pathways. Processing and quality-control states influence which transcripts are exported.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every newly made nuclear RNA immediately diffuses freely into the cytoplasm.
cards.prompt: What is Nuclear RNA Export? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Regulated nucleus-to-cytoplasm RNA transport.
Processing and surveillance affect export.

cards.definition: ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling changes nucleosome position, occupancy, or composition through molecular machines. It differs from covalent histone modification, though the processes can cooperate.
major_error_concepts: Treating nucleosome sliding as necessarily a DNA sequence mutation.
cards.prompt: What is Chromatin Remodeling? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Energy-dependent reorganization of nucleosomes.
Distinct from adding a covalent histone mark.

cards.definition: Polymerase proofreading removes some incorrectly added nucleotides during synthesis, commonly through a three-prime-to-five-prime exonuclease activity in proofreading DNA polymerases. This correction direction differs from the five-prime-to-three-prime synthesis direction.
major_error_concepts: Inferring that proofreading means DNA synthesis itself runs three-prime to five-prime.
cards.prompt: What is Polymerase Proofreading? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Removal of misincorporated nucleotides.
Distinguish correction direction from synthesis direction.

cards.definition: The spliceosome is an RNA-protein machinery that recognizes splice signals and catalyzes removal of many eukaryotic pre-mRNA introns. Its small nuclear RNAs contribute crucial recognition and catalytic roles.
major_error_concepts: Calling the spliceosome a DNA-cutting chromosome-editing complex.
cards.prompt: What is Spliceosome? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: RNA-protein complex for major classes of pre-mRNA splicing.
snRNAs have active roles.
